final_recommendation: The room converged on a comprehensive trilateral framework: 75% RVC with 40% independent labor-value verification, binding dairy quotas (20K metric tons, 20% cheese tariff), Chapter 19 dispute settlement intact, auto-renewal mechanism with continuity, and audit-first sequencing with automatic 90-day snapback. Legal counsel from all three parties entered drafting today to lock language word-for-word, targeting Friday signature pending Wednesday text confirmation.
minority_objections: Canada initially resisted trading both dairy AND Chapter 19 simultaneously, demanding one or the other move first
Supply-chain manufacturers raised concerns about retroactive RVC clawback risk during five-year phase-in if audits flag mid-restructuring failures
key_conflicts: U.S.-Mexico bilateral forming first created take-it-or-leave-it pressure on Canada (75% RVC non-negotiable)
Labor enforcement mechanism: text-only vs. independent factory audits with teeth became ratification blocker
40% labor-value formula ambiguity: subset of 75% RVC vs. independent calculation threatened to unravel package
Enforcement trigger sequencing: whether labor snapback, dairy review, and renewal continuity fire simultaneously or sequentially
key_concessions: U.S./Mexico: Five-year phase-in for Canadian auto suppliers to hit 75% RVC (number itself stayed fixed)
Canada: Agreed to binding dairy market access (20K metric tons fluid milk/yogurt, 20% cheese tariff cut) in exchange for Chapter 19 preservation
Mexico: Committed to independent factory-level wage audits with 90-day tariff snapback in binding text
U.S.: Auto-renewal mechanism with continuity (not hard sunset) to address business investment certainty
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain binding and enforceable, no carve-outs
Canada: Dairy supply management quotas must be in binding text, not 'subject to review'
U.S. Congress: Independent factory audits with automatic 90-day snapback, no self-reporting by Mexico
Labor: Wage verification and snapback must be in same enforcement mechanism, no decoupling
Auto industry: No retroactive RVC clawback; audit-first sequencing required before credit flows
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Congressional review timeline between Wednesday text delivery and Friday signature creates last-minute softening risk that multiple agents flagged but USTR did not fully address
Retroactive clawback risk for suppliers who fail audits mid-phase-in remains unresolved despite auto industry raising it twice
Synchronization complexity of three enforcement mechanisms (labor/dairy/renewal) in one legal text may surface contradictions Wednesday that kill Friday signature
downstream_risk_variables: Legal drafting room outcomes Wednesday: whether counsel actually locks language word-for-word or introduces 'subject to review' softening
Congressional ratification vote timing and political window: deal must close Friday or political momentum collapses
Mexico's domestic capacity to implement independent factory audits at scale within 90-day snapback timeline
Canadian Parliament's reaction to simultaneous dairy opening and Chapter 19 preservation package
Supply-chain restructuring costs and timeline: five-year phase-in assumes stable political/economic conditions
uncertainty_notes: Three critical gaps remain unresolved as legal drafting begins: (1) exact remediation window for suppliers who fail audits mid-restructuring (retroactive clawback vs. cure period); (2) whether Congress receives final binding text Thursday or if another markup round occurs before Friday; (3) synchronization mechanics when labor audit flags non-compliance—do dairy enforcement and renewal continuity reviews pause or proceed in parallel. These gaps could surface as contradictions Wednesday.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC non-negotiable from U.S.-Mexico bilateral drove Canada's phase-in demand; 40% labor-value formula ambiguity nearly collapsed package in R4; audit-first sequencing became binding requirement in R8
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress made independent audits + 90-day snapback a ratification requirement in R1; labor counsel entered drafting room in R5 to prevent softening; automatic trigger mechanism became deal-breaker in R7-R8
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada's dairy supply management was USTR's explicit price for phase-in (R1-R2); 20K metric tons + 20% cheese tariff became binding text requirement (R3-R8); dairy counsel entered legal room to prevent 'subject to review' softening
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated 'Chapter 19 or we walk' in R2; Mexico signaled flexibility if dairy moved (R2); USTR locked Chapter 19 binding in text as Canada's non-negotiable condition (R7-R8)
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply-chain raised hard sunset as investment-killing uncertainty in R2; USTR's auto-renewal mechanism with continuity (not termination) became locked requirement in R3-R5 to enable five-year restructuring commitments
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress stated labor enforcement as ratification blocker in R1; ratification risk drove labor counsel into drafting room (R5); Congressional review timeline (Wednesday text, Friday signature) became constraint on what could be softened (R7-R8)
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Raised as concern (restructuring costs, supplier reorganization, five-year phase-in timeline) in R1-R2 and R7-R8, but did not drive specific proposal changes—acknowledged as background constraint, not decisive factor
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: U.S.-Mexico bilateral terms (75% RVC, labor wage floor) became non-negotiable baseline in R1; USTR's 'sign Mexico's bilateral or get nothing' ultimatum created take-it-or-leave-it pressure that drove Canada's phase-in and dairy concessions
